lines.explanation: Before we read the very first symbol, the state is "outsite of a word" - so variable state is assigned to OUT

The condition of this loop will be true (i.e., evaluated to 1) when getchar is able to read a real character from standard input. If there are no more characters, getchar() will return EOF and the condition (EOF != EOF) will become false.
For any symbol read we increment nc counter - it counts total number of symbols read

This condition is true if the character read is a newline - '
'
For every newline character we increment nk counter 0 it counts lines
This condition is true if the character read is a newline, blank or tabulation
That means that we are  "outsite of a word" - so variable state is assigned to OUT
If the character read is not one of the "blanks" than we are moving through a word. This condition checks whethe we just have entered the word (i.e., on the previous letter we were "out")
If we are inside the word, the state is set to IN
Since we have just entered a word, we increment the word count.
There is no other else. If we are inside the word, but we also were inside when reading previous character, there is nothing to do - state is already IN and there is nothing to count.
